FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 26 February 1990, after 
the draft finalized by the Jute Mills Machinery/ Accessorie;s and Spare Parts Sectional Committee 
had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

This standard has been formulated to provide guidance to the manufacturers of pressing roller 
assembly for the jute drawing frame. This standard would ensure the manufacture of pressing 
roller assembly for jute drawing frame of acceptable quality. This standard mainly covers the 
requirements of flange which is the main working part of the pressing roller assembly. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : 21960 ^Rules for rounding ofT numerical values ( revised)\ The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



IS 12885 : 1990 



Indian Standard 



PRESSING ROLLER ASSEMBLY FOR JUTE 
DRAWING FRAME — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies requirements for 
pressing roller assembly for jute drawing frame. 

2 REFERENCES 

2,1 The following Indian Standards are 
necessary adjuncts to this standard. 

IS Mo. Title 

210 : 1972 Specification for grey iion 

castings ( third revision ) 

226 : 1975 Structural steel (standard 

quality [fifth revision ) 

1586 : 1968 Methods for Rockwell hard- 

ness test ( B and G scales ) for 
steel [first revision ) 

2500 Sampling inspection tables: 

( Part 1 ) : 1973 Part 1 Inspection by attributes 

and by count of defects [first 

revision ) 

3400 Method of test for vulcanised 

( Part 2 ) : 1980 rubber: Part 2 Hardness {first 
revision ) 

3 MANUFACTURE 

3.1 Pressing roller assembly shall consist of the 
following components: 

a) Flange, 

b) Boss, 

c) Axlc; 

d) Flanged axle nut, 

e) Housing for ball bearing, 

f ) Ball bearing, and 

g) Flange cot. 

3.1.1 The various components of pressing roller 
assembly shall be so manufactured as to give the 
pressing roller assembly which would satisfy the 
requirements given subsequently. 

3.2 Material 

3.2.1 Flange — cast iron conforming to grade 
FG 220 of IS 210 : 1978. 



3.2.2 Boss — cast iron conforming to grade 
FG 220 of IS 210 : 1978. 

3.2.3 Axle — miki steel conforming to IS 226 ; 
1975. 

3.2.4 Flanged Axle Nut — cast iron conforming to 
FG 220 of IS 210 : 1978. 

3.2.5 Housing for Ball Bearing — cast iron con- 
forming to FG 220 of IS 210 : 1978. 

3.2.6 Flange Cot — hardness of rubber shall be 
90 ± 5 IRHD ( same as shore A hardness ) when 
tested as per IS 3400 ( Part 2 ) : 1980. 

3.2.7 Ball Bearing — as agreed to between the 
buyer and the seller. 

4 DIMENSIONAL REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 Nominal Dimensions 

These shall be in accordance with the agreement 
between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 
In the absence of any agreement these shall be 
declared by the manufacturer. 

4.2 Tolerances 

The nominal dimensions shall be subject to the 
following tolerances [set Fig, 1 ):

5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

5.1 Assembly shall be able to run freely without 
generating any excessive frictional heat. 

5.2 The axle shall heat treated for achieving 
hardness of 45 ± ^HRC when tested in accor- 
dance with IS 1586 : 1968. 



1 



IS 19885: 1990 




Fig. 1 



All dimensions in millimetres. 

Pressing Roller Assembly for Drawing Frame 



5.3 The various components shall have inter- 
changeability with the components manufac- 
tured by the same manufacturer, 

5.4 There shall not be any wobble when various 
components are assembled to form assembly and 
the flange is set in motion. 

6 MARKING 

6,1 Each pressing roller assembly shall be legibly 
marked with the indication of the source of 
manufacture. 

6.1.1 The pressing roller assembly may also be 
marked with the Standard Mark. 



7 PACKING 

7.1 The pressing roller assembly shall be packed 
to ensure complete protection from rust. 

8 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CON- 
FORMITY 

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer to ascertain the 
conformity of the pressing roller assembly for 
jute drawing frame to the requirements of this 
specification, single sampling plan with Inspec- 
tion Level 1 and Acceptance Quality Level 
( AQL) of 1*5 percent given in Tables 1 and 2 
of IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1973 shall be followed. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 19S6 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with 
the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked 
products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safe- 
guard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted 
to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureaa of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification 
of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), 
BIS.
